source: Uploaded NBF Physics Grade 9 model textbook (2024), Chapter 1
note: Original draft questions aligned to chapter SLOs; teacher review recommended before publication. SLO codes reproduced as printed/extracted, including P-11 labels.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Which of the following is a physical quantity?
questions.e: Length can be measured and expressed with a unit.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Which statement best describes a physical quantity?
questions.e: A physical quantity is measurable.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Which of the following is a base physical quantity?
questions.e: Mass is one of the seven SI base quantities.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Which is a derived physical quantity?
questions.e: Velocity is derived from length divided by time.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: What is the SI base unit of electric current?
questions.e: The ampere (A) is the SI base unit of electric current.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Which pair correctly matches a base quantity and its SI unit?
questions.e: The kelvin (K) is the SI base unit of thermodynamic temperature.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The SI unit of area is:
questions.e: Area is length multiplied by length, so its unit is m².

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Write 0.00045 m in scientific notation.
questions.e: Move the decimal four places to the right to obtain 4.5, giving an exponent of −4.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: What is 3.2 × 10³ in ordinary decimal form?

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: How many metres are there in 5 kilometres?
questions.e: The prefix kilo means 1000; 5 km = 5000 m.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Which of the following is a scalar quantity?
questions.e: Speed has magnitude only, without direction.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Which quantity requires both magnitude and direction?
questions.e: Velocity is a vector because direction is part of its description.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A student walks 3 m east and then 4 m north. What is the magnitude of the displacement?
questions.e: The paths are at right angles, so the displacement is √(3² + 4²) = 5 m.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Which is a reasonable estimate for the length of an ordinary classroom?
questions.e: A classroom is typically several metres long; 8 m is a reasonable estimate.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Which instrument is most suitable for measuring the diameter of a thin wire?
questions.e: A micrometer screw gauge measures very small diameters precisely.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A measuring cylinder initially contains 30 mL of water. After a stone is immersed, it reads 42 mL. What is the stone’s volume?
questions.e: The displaced volume is 42 − 30 = 12 mL.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Which instrument is most suitable for measuring the time taken for a short race?
questions.e: A stopwatch measures elapsed time intervals.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Three readings of a length are 12.1 cm, 12.3 cm and 12.2 cm. What is their mean?

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A scale has 10 equal small divisions between 0 cm and 1 cm. What is its least count?
questions.e: Least count = 1 cm ÷ 10 = 0.1 cm.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A set of repeated readings are close to each other but far from the accepted value. The readings are:
questions.e: Closely grouped readings indicate precision; being far from the accepted value indicates poor accuracy.
